draft.title: The origins of Christianity
card: Christianity began in the first century CE. It grew out of the followers of Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish teacher who lived in Judea, a Roman province.
Jesus and his first followers were Jewish. After his death, his followers continued to spread his teachings, and they became a separate movement over time.
Followers such as Paul travelled to cities around the Mediterranean Sea and told others about Jesus. Small groups of believers formed in many places.
The Roman Empire helped the spread. Its roads, sea routes and shared languages made travel and communication easier.
draft.remember: Christianity began with Jewish followers of Jesus in Judea, then spread along Roman routes.

a.q: Where and among whom did Christianity begin?
opts: Among Jewish followers of Jesus in Judea
Among Roman officials in the city of Rome
Among Greek philosophers in Athens
Among traders along the Silk Road in Persia
a.why: Jesus was a Jewish teacher in Judea, and his first followers were Jewish. Rome later became important to the movement, but it was not where Christianity began.
a.clue: Think about where Jesus lived and who his first followers were.

b.q: Lydia is writing about how Christianity spread in the first century CE. Which point best explains why it spread so widely?
opts: Roman roads and sea routes made travel easier
Judea was far from any other region
Followers stayed in Judea and never travelled
Travel across the empire was very difficult
b.why: The empire's roads, sea routes and shared languages let followers such as Paul travel and share their message. The idea that followers stayed in Judea is wrong, because the card says they travelled to many cities.
b.clue: Think about how the empire helped people move and communicate.

a.best: Among Jewish followers of Jesus in Judea

b.best: Roman roads and sea routes made travel easier

problems.detail: The three wrong options are plainly absurd or contradict the question itself ("never travelled" for a question about wide spread, "travel was very difficult", "far from any other region"). A Year 11 student can pick the answer without knowing the idea. Plausible distractors would test it better, such as Christianity being made the official religion at once, or spreading mainly through Persia.

proposal.title: The origins of Christianity
card: Christianity began in the first century CE among the followers of Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish teacher in Judea, a Roman province. His first followers were Jewish too.
After his death, followers such as Paul travelled to cities around the Mediterranean Sea and told others about Jesus. Over time the movement became separate from Judaism.
The Roman Empire helped the spread. Its roads, sea routes and shared languages made travel and communication easier.
For its first centuries, Christianity was a small minority faith, at times persecuted by Roman rulers. It became the empire's official religion only in the late 300s CE.
proposal.remember: Christianity began with Jewish followers of Jesus in Judea, then spread slowly along Roman routes.

opts: Among Jewish followers of Jesus in Judea

a.why: Jesus was a Jewish teacher in Judea, and his first followers were Jewish. Rome later became important to the movement, but it was not where Christianity began.

b.q: Lydia is writing about how Christianity spread in the first century CE. Which point best explains its spread?
opts: Followers used Roman roads and sea routes to travel
The emperor made it the official religion at once
Followers carried it mainly east through Persia
Roman soldiers were ordered to spread it in new lands
b.why: Followers such as Paul used the empire's roads, sea routes and shared languages to reach cities around the Mediterranean. It was not made official at once: it stayed a small, sometimes persecuted faith until the late 300s CE.
b.clue: Who spread the message, and what did the empire give them?
